lesson.x: En anglais, deux temps du présent s'emploient souvent : le present simple (habitudes, vérités générales) et le present continuous (action en cours).
Present simple : base verbale, avec -s à la 3e personne du singulier : I play, he plays, she watches, it goes.
Négation : do not (don't) / does not (doesn't) + base verbale : He doesn't play. Question : Do you play ? Does she play ?
Marqueurs du present simple : always, usually, often, sometimes, never, every day, on Mondays.
Present continuous : to be (am / is / are) + verbe en -ing : I am playing, she is reading, they are eating.
Négation : I am not playing. Question : Are you playing ?
Marqueurs du present continuous : now, at the moment, today, right now.
Orthographe du -ing : run → running, write → writing, play → playing.
Exemple : He plays football every Saturday (habitude), but he is studying now (en cours).
Les verbes d'état (know, like, love, want) ne s'emploient pas à la forme -ing.
